## Household and background

Reese Falconer (born July 23, 1994) is single with no dependents, renting at 902 Foundry Lane in Anytown. Weekdays he is a warehouse lead at Granite Peak Warehousing — one W-2, box 1 wages $43,617.00, box 2 federal withholding $3,940.00.

Evenings and weekends he drives food and package deliveries for the Dashly platform, which reported $21,380.00 of payouts on a Form 1099-NEC (box 1 — his only gig income source). His mileage log shows 14,400 delivery miles of 18,000 total miles on the car (80% business use), and his receipts total $6,145.00 of gas, oil, repairs, insurance, and registration for the year. He claims the ACTUAL-EXPENSE vehicle method because he has no choice of method left: in the car's FIRST year of business use he deducted actual expenses, and under the Pub 463 first-year rule a car must be on the standard mileage rate in its first business year to ever use that rate — so this car is locked into actual expenses. He still keeps the mileage log because the business-use percentage sets the deductible share of the operating costs. Other business costs — the dedicated phone plan, insulated bags, and supplies — came to $1,872.00. He made no estimated tax payments and knows the self-employment tax means he will owe in April.

## Interview

**Q.** Is the 1099-NEC your only gig income?

**A.** Yes — everything comes through the Dashly platform; the $21,380 on the 1099 is all of my receipts.

**Q.** Which vehicle-expense method do you want — standard mileage or actual expenses?

**A.** Actual expenses — that's the only method this car can use. I took actual expenses in its first year of business use, and my preparer told me that means I can't ever switch it to the standard mileage rate. I kept every receipt — $6,145 — and my log shows 14,400 of 18,000 miles were deliveries.

**Q.** Did the platform withhold any tax, or did you pay estimated taxes?

**A.** No withholding and no estimated payments. I know self-employment tax is on top of income tax — I've been setting aside money for the April bill.

**Q.** Any dependents? Could anyone claim you as a dependent? Are you blind, disabled, or a student? A U.S. citizen all year?

**A.** No to all of those, and yes — citizen all year.

## Preparer notes

- Vehicle method is FORCED, not chosen for advantage: actual expenses were deducted in the car's first year of business use, and Pub 463 requires a car to use the standard mileage rate in its FIRST business year to ever use that rate — this car is therefore locked into actual expenses for its remaining business life. The mileage log is still kept: it fixes the business-use percentage (14,400 ÷ 18,000 = 80%) that scales the deductible operating costs.
- Line 9 (actual-expense method) = 80% × 6,145 = 4,916; net profit = 21,380 − 1,872 − 4,916 = 14,592 → Schedule 1 line 3 → 1040 line 8.

The W-2 social security wages (43,617) leave ample room under the 176,100 wage base.
